shouldFix.title: Combined-schema precedence ignores populated severity arrays and still permits finding erasure
evidence: selection always chooses combinedFindingsArray when findings is an object array, even if blockers, shouldFix, or advisories is also an object array. The combined branch then examines those three members only when they are integers; object arrays are silently ignored.

A probe with findings=[], blockers=[{id:B,severity:BLOCKER}], shouldFix=[], and advisories=[] selects combinedFindingsArray, extracts no ids, has an integer-count sum of zero, and satisfies the stated empty-extraction rule. The populated blocker array disappears.
A nonempty variant also passes: findings=[{id:A,severity:ADVISORY}], blockers=[{id:B,severity:BLOCKER}], shouldFix=0, advisories=1 extracts only A and passes 1=0+1 while silently dropping B.

The severity-array branch likewise ignores an invalid negative integer on a skipped key whenever another array supplies a nonempty extraction; only a positive skipped integer is stated to refuse. These probes are recognized rather than routed to the unrecognized-schema refusal.
All actual pinned v8-v17 verdicts use one schema shape consistently and extract correctly, so no current finding is erased. The defect remains SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A partially written, schema-transition, or hostile frozen verdict can carry blocker or SHOULD-FIX objects in severity arrays while an empty or smaller findings[] array wins selection. Successor coverage then certifies an incomplete id set, preserving the finding-erasure path HAE17-CX-01 was meant to close.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Make the schemas mutually exclusive and validate all relevant member types before extraction. When findings[] selects the combined schema, require each present blockers/shouldFix/advisories member to be a nonnegative integer count and REFUSE any array or other type. When severityArrays is selected, require findings to be absent and each present severity member to be an object array or the explicitly allowed zero count; REFUSE negative integers and every other mixed shape.

shouldFix.title: The combined-findings cross-check validates only a grand total, so source severity can be laundered into a non-blocking register disposition
evidence: HAE17-CX-01 required available integer counts to be cross-checked against extracted severity totals. v18 instead says only that the extracted id count MUST equal the sum of the integer blockers, shouldFix, and advisories counts.

A combined-schema probe with findings=[{id:B,severity:BLOCKER},{id:S,severity:SHOULD-FIX}], blockers=0, shouldFix=2, and advisories=0 passes the literal v18 rule because two extracted ids equal the summed count two, even though the blocker and SHOULD-FIX category totals are each wrong.
combinedFindingsArray extracts only object.id, and laneCheck/pairCheck compare only id sets. The frozen finding severity is therefore discarded before the register is checked.

A disposition-laundering probe changes the registered HAE17-CX-01 disposition from REPAIRED to ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING and removes its honestyRepairsFromV17 entry. laneCheck still passes because the id remains present; fromVnCheck also passes because it trusts the mutated register disposition. The pinned frozen verdict still says HAE17-CX-01 is SHOULD-FIX, but no governing check compares that source severity with the register disposition.

All actual pinned v8-v17 lanes are sound: their schemas are recognized, every id and (lane,id) pair reproduces, each current source severity is compatible with its actual register disposition, and every FromVN prefix exactly equals the REPAIRED register set. The defect is in the standing mechanical rule, so it is SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A future successor can preserve finding-id coverage while downgrading a frozen BLOCKER or SHOULD-FIX to ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING, thereby omitting it from the repair ledger and still passing every stated coverage check. That defeats the rule's purpose and can support a false 0/0 lineage claim.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Retain source severity during extraction: derive it from findings[].severity for combinedFindingsArray and from the blockers/shouldFix/advisories array key for severityArrays. Compare each present integer counter independently with the derived count for that severity, refusing unknown or mismatched severity. Make register coverage compare (lane,id,severity), or otherwise explicitly require a frozen BLOCKER/SHOULD-FIX to have a repair-requiring disposition and forbid ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING for it. Keep FromVN equality coupled to that validated disposition.
